terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Not solved and deliberately not matched to the reference. The review camera is fixed by the consumer harness (scripts/breadlab.ts applyView).

objectClass.notes: Matte faceted clay shading, flat color facets only -- prompt JSON explicitly excludes any shine. Consumer runtime is a stylized low-poly showcase, so target look is faceted matte clay rather than food photorealism.

reasoning: Single macro body (chestnut-shell) with one meso sub-region (chestnut-base-patch), scoring componentCount 1.
Silhouette is one revolved onion-dome with a mild belly-base taper and one crease, scoring silhouetteComplexity 1.
No repetition system: a single instance, not a cluster, scoring repetitionDensity 0.
One material family in two albedo zones (shell vs base patch), so materialLayerCount scores 1.
Local detail density scores 1: the split-line crease is the one authored micro-feature, carried geometrically rather than as a color bucket.
Occlusion risk scores 1: the far side (opposite the crease) is hidden but fully inferable by radial symmetry.
Action readiness scores 0: static turntable showcase prop, no pivots/sockets/colliders beyond a bounding proxy.
Aggregate 5/24 with no axis above 1 confirms the simple tier.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier by part count, but still needs meso depth (the base patch is a separately shaded sub-region split from the shell) even though there is no repetition system (single instance, not a cluster).

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The far side of the dome (opposite the split-line crease) is never directly visible at any reviewed azimuth; resolved by construction (full radial symmetry before the crease indent).
The runtime normalizes the longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary and only the authored ratios carry meaning.
The split-line crease position is not identity-critical at pixel precision; its presence and camera-facing orientation are what the review scores.

collider.notes: Spherical bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

componentTree.name: Chestnut shell (dome + crease)
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous, smoothly varying rotationally symmetric mass -- an onion-dome shell revolved from a single monotonic-then-tapering profile, poles at apex and base center. Decision tree step 6. Not a sphere/cone primitive because the reference shows a distinct belly-wider-than-base taper and a sharp (not rounded) apex, which only a custom profile carries.

deformationStack.notes: Single-sector (sector 5 of 16, azimuth ~112.5-135deg, facing the harness three-quarter camera) radius indent across rings [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], multiplying local radius by (1 - 0.08). Carries the reference's #C68B5B split-line hue as a geometric facet-shading seam instead of a third material bucket (mesh<=2 budget, types.ts section 1).

Uniform per-vertex position noise, amplitude 0.018 (0.036 of equatorial radius), applied while the shell is still indexed so the base-patch/shell shared triangle boundary moves together and never tears (R1).

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: dome (polar top-down) projection per material bucket (scripts/breads/lib.ts uvDome) -- no texture is emitted, UVs exist only for merge attribute consistency
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: flat normals baked by splitting vertices after jitter, never a flatShading flag

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Hard consumer budget for the 'single' ingredient group: 200-500 tri and <=48KB target (types.ts R2), hard ceiling <=2500 tri and <=100KB (scripts/check-budget.mjs). Target reached by construction (16 segments x 8 profile transitions = 224 tri before crease displacement, which adds zero triangles), not by decimation.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2), intensity 1.4, upper-left -- the same relationship as the reference's 'single soft key light upper-left'.
lightingFromPhoto.usage: Fixed by scripts/breadlab.ts, mirrored from scripts/thumbsHarness.ts. Not authored by the model.
lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control and no tone mapping -- authored albedo lands on screen almost unchanged.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 -- a high ambient ratio, which is why the lower-dome darkening and the crease seam rely on the shell's own curvature turning away from the key light rather than a painted shadow tone.
lightingFromPhoto.contactShadow: none -- no shadow map, no ground plane rendered.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Cool directional fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2), intensity 0.2, opposite the key.
lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: NoToneMapping (three.js default); no AO available on the runtime Lambert material.

proceduralStrategy: Revolve the shell from the shared belly-taper profile (pole at base center, base edge, belly, apex pole).
Indent one fixed sector's radius across the mid-profile rings before jitter to carry the split-line crease as facet shading.
Jitter vertices while the shell is still indexed, so the base-patch/shell split never tears.
Bake faceting by splitting vertices and recomputing normals; never request flatShading.
Slice the base-cap fan (pole-to-base-edge) into its own triangle range after facet() for the base-patch material.
Project dome UVs per bucket, then merge by material into exactly two meshes.
Translate the whole shell's own bounding box floor to world Y=0.
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-body rotation for the showcase turntable
destructionAnchors: single fractureGroup; no plausible sub-fracture for a whole chestnut

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/chestnut.json names a third hue (#5E4029) for the shaded lower half, which this spec does not wire to a material bucket.
risks.mitigation: mesh<=2 budget forces a 2-bucket split (types.ts section 1); the runtime key light already darkens the lower dome of a convex shell for free via N.L falloff. Shell bucket carries #7A5638 everywhere except the base-patch fan.

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/chestnut.json names a fourth hue (#C68B5B) for the split-line seam, which this spec does not wire to a material bucket.
risks.mitigation: Carried as a geometric sector-local radius indent (CREASE_SECTOR) instead -- the two new facet edges catch the key light differently, reading as a lighter/darker seam through shading rather than paint. Sector chosen to face the harness review camera (azimuth ~121.8deg).

risks.description: Any vertex-color-based region paint is silently discarded by the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap, collapsing the two-tone split to one flat tone.
risks.mitigation: The shell/base-patch split is carried by two separate materials on two separate triangle ranges from one shared indexed shell, split by triangle index. No vertexPaint block is authored anywhere in this spec.

risks.description: A flatShading flag is not inherited by the runtime material swap, so a model relying on it renders smooth.
risks.mitigation: Faceting is baked into geometry by splitting vertices (scripts/breads/lib.ts facet) before export.

risks.description: Base-patch and shell triangles come from the same shell; jittering after the triangle-range slice (rather than before) would let the shared boundary vertices move independently and open a crack.
risks.mitigation: Jitter runs once, on the whole indexed shell, before facet()/slice -- both buckets read the same already-jittered positions.

risks.description: mergeByMaterial throws when geometries in one bucket carry different attribute sets.
risks.mitigation: Every geometry gets exactly position, normal and uv; no color attribute is ever created; both part geometries route through the same uvDome call.
